Summary: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview on November 12, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind its AI chip design platform. The company says the model scored 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, ahead of several open-weight rivals, and that its full R&D cost was $32M.
Why it matters: Developers choosing open-weight models for coding agents may weigh Ricursive's claimed low training cost and its claim that the model runs on local hardware such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.

Story 2
Headline: ReTrace turns agent runs into workflows where code, not an LLM, picks each step
Card: ReTrace: coded workflows replace LLM step-picking, at 24% lower cost per task
Narration: Researchers present ReTrace, which turns agent runs into workflows where code, not a language model, chooses each step. The authors say it cuts cost per task by twenty-four percent, though it trails the agent slightly on accuracy.
Summary: Researchers present ReTrace, a method that turns a standard operating procedure and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow. The authors say LLM agents call a model to choose every step, which adds latency and cost at scale, and ReTrace lets code select the next step instead. In their reported tests on 79 procedures, ReTrace workflows reached 93.8% completion versus 96.8% for the agent, at 24% lower cost per task.
Why it matters: Teams running many automated business procedures could cut cost per task and latency if coded workflows keep most of an agent's accuracy.

Headline: LeRobot v0.7.0 adds streamed-data training and interactive robot control
Card: LeRobot v0.7.0: train on streamed data, steer robots from the terminal

The release also adds interactive rollouts for switching subtasks and steering a running robot from the terminal, plus four world action models and four new VLA models. The Hub now hosts almost 300 TB of open physical AI data in LeRobot format.
Why it matters: Robotics developers can train on large open datasets without local copies, and run policies on a remote GPU while the robot's own computer handles cameras and motors.
